focus: Exodus 26 gives the pattern for the tabernacle itself: its inner curtains, its tent and coverings, and the gold-covered frame that holds it up. The chapter then describes the veil that divides the holy place from the Most Holy, where the ark and mercy seat will stand, and the screen at the tent’s entrance.

sections.title: The Inner Curtains Joined into One Tabernacle
sections.summary: Ten curtains of fine linen in blue, purple, and scarlet, woven with cherubim, are joined in two sets of five. Fifty gold clasps couple the sets together, “so that it may be one tabernacle” (Exodus 26:6).

sections.title: The Tent of Goats’ Hair and Its Coverings
sections.summary: Eleven curtains of goats’ hair, joined with bronze clasps, form a tent over the tabernacle, with the extra length hanging over the back and sides. Above them go a covering of ram skins dyed red and a covering of badger skins.

sections.title: The Gold-Covered Frame of Boards, Sockets, and Bars
sections.summary: Upright boards of acacia wood stand in silver sockets on the south, north, and west sides, with special boards for the corners, and they are held together by bars, with a middle bar running from end to end. Boards and bars are overlaid with gold, and Moses is to raise the tabernacle “according to its pattern which you were shown on the mountain” (Exodus 26:30).

sections.title: The Veil Divides the Holy Place from the Most Holy
sections.summary: A veil woven with cherubim hangs on four gold-covered pillars, and the ark of the Testimony is placed behind it, for the veil is “a divider for you between the holy place and the Most Holy” (Exodus 26:33). The mercy seat is placed on the ark in the Most Holy, and the table and lampstand stand outside the veil.

sections.title: The Screen for the Door of the Tabernacle
sections.summary: A woven screen of blue, purple, and scarlet thread and fine linen is made for the door of the tabernacle. It hangs on five gold-covered pillars set in bronze sockets.

1.brief: Israel is to make the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine woven linen in blue, purple, and scarlet, woven with designs of cherubim. The innermost covering of God’s dwelling is made of the finest materials.
1.explain:
“Moreover you shall make the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine woven linen and blue, purple, and scarlet thread;”

“The tabernacle” here means the inner dwelling itself, made of “ten curtains” of the finest linen and colored thread. This is the innermost covering, seen from inside the holy places.

“with artistic designs of cherubim you shall weave them.”

“Cherubim” are woven into the curtains. Priests inside the tent would see heavenly guardians all around them. The innermost covering of God’s dwelling is made of the finest materials.

2.brief: Each curtain is twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide, all the same size. The uniform measurements reflect careful obedience to God’s pattern.
2.explain:
“The length of each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits.”

Each curtain was about 42 feet long and 6 feet wide.

“And every one of the curtains shall have the same measurements.”

All are the same size. The uniform measurements reflect careful obedience to God’s pattern.

3.brief: Five curtains are joined together, and the other five are joined together. The curtains form two large sets.
3.explain:
“Five curtains shall be coupled to one another, and the other five curtains shall be coupled to one another.”

The ten curtains are sewn into two large sets of five each.

4.brief: Loops of blue yarn are made on the edge of the last curtain in each set. The loops prepare the two sets to be joined.
4.explain:
“And you shall make loops of blue yarn on the edge of the curtain on the selvedge of one set,”

“Loops of blue yarn” are sewn on the edge of one set.

“and likewise you shall do on the outer edge of the other curtain of the second set.”

Matching loops go on the second set. The loops prepare the two sets to be joined.

5.brief: Fifty loops are made on each set, placed opposite one another. The matching loops allow a precise joining.
5.explain:
“Fifty loops you shall make in the one curtain, and fifty loops you shall make on the edge of the curtain that is on the end of the second set,”

Each set has “fifty loops.”

“that the loops may be clasped to one another.”

The loops line up opposite each other. The matching loops allow a precise joining.

6.brief: Fifty gold clasps couple the curtains together, “so that it may be one tabernacle.” The many pieces form a single dwelling for God.
6.explain:
“And you shall make fifty clasps of gold, and couple the curtains together with the clasps,”

“Fifty clasps of gold” join the two sets.

“so that it may be one tabernacle.”

The many pieces form “one tabernacle,” a single dwelling for God.

7.brief: Eleven curtains of goats’ hair are made to form a tent over the tabernacle. A protective layer is placed over the inner curtains.
7.explain:
“You shall also make curtains of goats’ hair, to be a tent over the tabernacle.”

Over the linen dwelling goes “a tent” of “goats’ hair,” a coarse, dark, durable fabric used for Bedouin tents.

“You shall make eleven curtains.”

There are “eleven” of these curtains, one more than the linen ones. A protective layer is placed over the inner curtains.

8.brief: Each goats’ hair curtain is thirty cubits long and four cubits wide, all the same size. The outer curtains are longer so they can cover the inner ones.
8.explain:
“The length of each curtain shall be thirty cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits;”

These curtains are “thirty cubits” long, two cubits longer than the linen ones, so they can hang lower and cover them.

“and the eleven curtains shall all have the same measurements.”

All are the same size.

9.brief: Five curtains are joined together and six together, and the sixth is doubled over at the front of the tent. The arrangement fits the covering to the structure.
9.explain:
“And you shall couple five curtains by themselves and six curtains by themselves,”

They are joined into sets of five and six.

“and you shall double over the sixth curtain at the forefront of the tent.”

The extra curtain is folded over at “the forefront,” the front of the tent. The arrangement fits the covering to the structure.

10.brief: Fifty loops are made on the edge of the outermost curtain of each set. The tent is prepared for joining like the inner curtains.
10.explain:
“You shall make fifty loops on the edge of the curtain that is outermost in one set, and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain of the second set.”

The tent sets are given loops like the inner curtains.

11.brief: Fifty bronze clasps join the tent together “that it may be one.” The outer tent, like the inner dwelling, forms one whole.
11.explain:
“And you shall make fifty bronze clasps, put the clasps into the loops,”

Here the clasps are “bronze,” not gold. The less precious metal is used farther from God’s presence.

“and couple the tent together, that it may be one.”

The outer tent, like the inner dwelling, forms one whole.

12.brief: The extra half curtain hangs over the back of the tabernacle. The covering is fitted to protect the whole structure.
12.explain:
“The remnant that remains of the curtains of the tent, the half curtain that remains, shall hang over the back of the tabernacle.”

The extra length of the goats’ hair tent “shall hang over the back.” The covering is fitted to protect the whole structure.

13.brief: A cubit of the extra length hangs over each side to cover it. Every side of the dwelling is protected.
13.explain:
“And a cubit on one side and a cubit on the other side, of what remains of the length of the curtains of the tent,”

The extra two cubits of length divide into one cubit on each side.

“shall hang over the sides of the tabernacle, on this side and on that side, to cover it.”

These hang down “to cover it.” Every side of the dwelling is protected.

14.brief: A covering of ram skins dyed red is made for the tent, with a covering of badger skins above it. The outer layers shield the sanctuary from the weather.
14.explain:
“You shall also make a covering of ram skins dyed red for the tent,”

A third layer of “ram skins dyed red” goes over the goats’ hair.

“and a covering of badger skins above that.”

A fourth, outermost layer of “badger skins” (see the note at 25:5) completes the roof. The outer layers shield the sanctuary from the weather. From outside, the tabernacle looked plain. Its beauty was within.

15.brief: Upright boards of acacia wood are made for the tabernacle. The boards form the frame that holds up the curtains.
15.explain:
“And for the tabernacle you shall make the boards of acacia wood, standing upright.”

“Boards” or frames “of acacia wood” stand upright to form the walls. The boards form the frame that holds up the curtains.
15.notes: Some interpreters think the Hebrew word translated “boards” describes open frames rather than solid planks, which would have been lighter to carry and would let the inner curtains show through. The text does not settle the question.

16.brief: Each board is ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide. The frame is built to exact measurements.
16.explain:
“Ten cubits shall be the length of a board, and a cubit and a half shall be the width of each board.”

Each board is about 15 feet tall and 27 inches wide. The frame is built to exact measurements.

17.brief: Each board has two tenons for joining it to the next. The boards are designed to fit firmly together.
17.explain:
“Two tenons shall be in each board for binding one to another.”

Each board has “two tenons,” projections at the bottom that fit into sockets.

“Thus you shall make for all the boards of the tabernacle.”

Every board is made the same way. The boards fit firmly together.

18.brief: Twenty boards are made for the south side. The frame begins with its longest wall.
18.explain:
“And you shall make the boards for the tabernacle, twenty boards for the south side.”

“Twenty boards” form the south wall. The frame begins with its longest wall.

19.brief: Forty silver sockets are made, two under each board for its tenons. The frame rests on a foundation of silver.
19.explain:
“You shall make forty sockets of silver under the twenty boards:”

“Forty sockets of silver” serve as bases for the twenty boards.

“two sockets under each of the boards for its two tenons.”

Each board rests on two sockets. The frame rests on a foundation of silver.
19.notes: The silver came from the atonement money paid by each counted Israelite (30:11–16; 38:25–28). Each socket used a talent of silver.

20.brief: Twenty boards are made for the north side. The second long wall matches the first.
20.explain:
“And for the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, there shall be twenty boards”

The north wall also has “twenty boards.” The second long wall matches the first.

21.brief: The north side also has forty silver sockets, two under each board. Both long sides rest on silver.
21.explain:
“and their forty sockets of silver: two sockets under each of the boards.”

The north side rests on forty silver sockets.

22.brief: Six boards are made for the far side, toward the west. The rear wall closes the structure.
22.explain:
“For the far side of the tabernacle, westward, you shall make six boards.”

The back wall faces “westward.” The entrance therefore faces east. The rear wall closes the structure.
22.notes: The entrance faced east, toward the rising sun. Eden was entered from the east, where the cherubim guarded the way (Genesis 3:24).

23.brief: Two boards are made for the back corners. The corners are specially strengthened.
23.explain:
“And you shall also make two boards for the two back corners of the tabernacle.”

Two special boards form “the two back corners.” The corners are specially strengthened.

24.brief: The corner boards are coupled at the bottom and joined at the top by one ring. The corners hold the frame together.
24.explain:
“They shall be coupled together at the bottom and they shall be coupled together at the top by one ring.”

The corner boards are joined “at the bottom” and “at the top by one ring.”

“Thus it shall be for both of them. They shall be for the two corners.”

Both corners are made alike. The corners hold the frame together.

25.brief: The back wall has eight boards with sixteen silver sockets, two under each board. The rear of the frame rests on silver like the long sides.
25.explain:
“So there shall be eight boards with their sockets of silver—sixteen sockets—two sockets under each of the boards.”

The back wall has “eight boards” in all, six plus two corner boards, on “sixteen sockets.” The rear of the frame rests on silver like the long sides.

26.brief: Bars of acacia wood are made, five for the boards on one side. The bars hold the boards in line.
26.explain:
“And you shall make bars of acacia wood: five for the boards on one side of the tabernacle,”

Horizontal “bars” hold the boards in line. Five are made for one side.

27.brief: Five bars are made for the other side and five for the west side. All three walls are braced.
27.explain:
“five bars for the boards on the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the side of the tabernacle, for the far side westward.”

Five more bars are made for each of the other two walls. All three walls are braced.

28.brief: The middle bar runs through the boards from end to end. The central bar binds the whole wall together.
28.explain:
“The middle bar shall pass through the midst of the boards from end to end.”

“The middle bar” runs the full length of each wall. The central bar binds the whole wall together.

29.brief: The boards are overlaid with gold, with gold rings to hold the bars, and the bars are overlaid with gold. The frame of God’s dwelling shines with gold.
29.explain:
“You shall overlay the boards with gold, make their rings of gold as holders for the bars, and overlay the bars with gold.”

The boards and bars are overlaid with gold, and the rings that hold the bars are made of gold. The frame of God’s dwelling shines with gold inside.

30.brief: Moses is to raise up the tabernacle “according to its pattern which you were shown on the mountain.” The whole structure must follow God’s design exactly.
30.explain:
“And you shall raise up the tabernacle according to its pattern which you were shown on the mountain.”

The section ends as 25:9 and 25:40 did. Moses must build “according to its pattern.” The arrangement serves God’s purpose to dwell with Israel in the form He appoints.

31.brief: A veil is made of blue, purple, and scarlet thread and fine linen, woven with cherubim. The veil will guard the most holy place.
31.explain:
“You shall make a veil woven of blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and fine woven linen.”

“A veil” of the same rich materials as the inner curtains is woven.

“It shall be woven with an artistic design of cherubim.”

Like the curtains, it bears “cherubim.” As cherubim guarded the way to the tree of life (Genesis 3:24), these woven cherubim guard the way into God’s innermost presence. The veil will guard the most holy place.

32.brief: The veil hangs on four gold-covered pillars of acacia wood with gold hooks and silver sockets. The veil is hung with great care and honor.
32.explain:
“You shall hang it upon the four pillars of acacia wood overlaid with gold.”

The veil hangs on “four pillars” overlaid with gold.

“Their hooks shall be gold, upon four sockets of silver.”

The pillars have “gold” hooks and stand on “silver” sockets. The veil is hung with great care and honor.

33.brief: The veil hangs from the clasps, and the ark of the Testimony is placed behind it, for the veil divides the holy place from the Most Holy. The veil separates God’s innermost dwelling, and Hebrews 10:19–20 later speaks of the way through the veil opened by Christ.
33.explain:
“And you shall hang the veil from the clasps.”

The veil hangs beneath “the clasps” that join the two sets of inner curtains (26:6).

“Then you shall bring the ark of the Testimony in there, behind the veil.”

The ark is hidden from view.

“The veil shall be a divider for you between the holy place and the Most Holy.”

The veil is “a divider” between “the holy place” and “the Most Holy.” It separates God’s innermost dwelling from everything else. Only the high priest could pass through, once a year, and not without blood (Leviticus 16:2, 12–15; Hebrews 9:6–7). When Jesus died, “the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom” (Matthew 27:51). Hebrews 10:19–20 says believers have “boldness to enter the Holiest by the blood of Jesus, by a new and living way which He consecrated for us, through the veil, that is, His flesh.” The way into God’s presence that the veil closed is now open through Christ.

34.brief: The mercy seat is placed on the ark of the Testimony in the Most Holy. God’s meeting place stands behind the veil.
34.explain:
“You shall put the mercy seat upon the ark of the Testimony in the Most Holy.”

The mercy seat sits on the ark in “the Most Holy.” God’s meeting place stands behind the veil.
34.notes: The Most Holy Place was ten cubits in each direction, a perfect cube. The Most Holy Place in Solomon’s temple was also a cube (1 Kings 6:20).

35.brief: The table is set outside the veil on the north side and the lampstand across from it on the south side. The holy place is arranged in front of the Most Holy.
35.explain:
“You shall set the table outside the veil,”

The table stands “outside the veil,” in the holy place.

“and the lampstand across from the table on the side of the tabernacle toward the south; and you shall put the table on the north side.”

The table is on the north side and the lampstand on the south, facing each other. The holy place is arranged in front of the Most Holy. The incense altar (30:1–6) will stand directly before the veil.

36.brief: A screen is made for the door of the tabernacle, woven in blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen. The entrance to the tent has its own covering.
36.explain:
“You shall make a screen for the door of the tabernacle,”

“A screen” covers “the door,” the entrance of the tent on the east side. It is distinct from the inner veil.

“woven of blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and fine woven linen, made by a weaver.”

The screen is woven in the same colors but “made by a weaver,” with embroidered work rather than the cherubim design of the veil. The entrance to the tent has its own covering.

37.brief: Five pillars of acacia wood overlaid with gold, with gold hooks and five bronze sockets, are made for the screen. The pillars support the entrance to the tent.
37.explain:
“And you shall make for the screen five pillars of acacia wood, and overlay them with gold;”

The screen hangs on “five pillars” overlaid with gold.

“their hooks shall be gold, and you shall cast five sockets of bronze for them.”

These pillars stand on “bronze” sockets, not silver. Bronze marks the transition from the tent to the courtyard, where the bronze altar stands. The pillars support the entrance to the tent.
